summary.text: How to set up auditors on the same sign-in page, which groups to use, and where to change settings.

0.text: Everyone logs in to the same login page. There is no separate examiner portal. Menus and rights come from the groups you assign. This corresponds to the Thoropass model: an examiner examines evidence; An audit administrator (management) can also set up other auditors. Identity administrators create accounts that are not validators. This is not the job of an auditor.

1.text: Demonstration environments include three starting accounts so you can try out each task. Change these passwords before each joint demonstration. Production environments create their own people and assign them to the groups below. This guide describes how to set up the product. It is not a certification claim.

0.text: Open the local IAM administration and create or select the person.

1.text: Add the person to the groups for their role in the table below.

2.text: Or create them with the matching enrollment template.

3.text: Ask them to sign in on the normal sign-in page.

4.text: Open audit engagements to invite them to an engagement if your process uses invitations.

gateIntro.text: OpenAPI and Swagger UI are limited to Super Administrators and members of the well-known Developers group (

gateIntroAfter.text: ). Ordinary admins and auditors do not receive this class.

honestyAlert.text: Technical reference for super administrators and developers. Use Swagger / OpenAPI for current route forms. Auth models follow docs/auth-architecture.md (admin session/token, agent-HMAC dual_mode inflow, enrollment bootstrap rest). The OpenAPI download is not a FedRAMP, CMMC, or FIPS certification package.

audience.text: This class is aimed at API users and developers who integrate with AIC Server. Operator runbooks are located under admin manuals. Assessor procedures lie beneath auditor manuals. Prefer those classes when the task is configuration or proof checking and not route forms.

howTo[0].text: Open Swagger UI to check authenticated routes with your current session cookie or admin token header as documented in the security schemas.

howTo[1].text: Download OpenAPI JSON for offline testing or client generation. Get it again after each server deployment, the routes changed.

howTo[2].text: Agent wire routes expect HMAC headers when agents sign. Unsigned is accepted only while AGENT_HMAC_ENFORCE_MODE=dual_mode applies.

howTo[3].text: Startup wizard admin routes live under /api/admin/startup-wizard. Storage paths for messaging secrets stay in AppConfig — never in wizard response JSON.

howTo[4].text: Prefer docs under /docs/admin for operator runbooks. This page is for API users and developers.

limits[0].text: OpenAPI coverage follows declared routes. A missing operation in the UI is not proven just by downloading this file.

limits[1].text: Dual-mode agent HMAC is a run-in stance, not an assertion that every agent is already signed.

limits[2].text: Don’t treat successful Swagger calls as evidence of a completed ATO — keep this work in the assessment binder and in your SSP process.

intro.text: Live view of the three AIC Server process logs. Application tracing is on stderr (service capture) and the rolling application log file. stdout is usually empty. Secrets are masked. Debug stays off unless you choose Debug or Trace.

policyHelper.text: Keep live logs for the number of days you set, or until they reach the size limit. Then they rotate into a ZIP archive. They are not dropped silently.

archivesEmpty.text: No archives yet. Rotate a live stream, or wait until a file reaches the size or age limit.

deleteConfirmBody.text: This permanently deletes {{name}}. The action is recorded in the audit log.

clearConfirmBody.text: This truncates the on-disk stdout, stderr, and application (rolling) log files and clears this view. Only entries written after you confirm will be shown. Archived ZIP files are not deleted.

restartConfirmBody.text: Schedules a service stop and start so you can capture a fresh start banner in the logs.

noLines.text: No log lines in this view. Try All levels, switch streams, or wait for new output.

fileMissing.text: Log file does not exist yet. Start or restart the service, then click Reload tail.

policyFailed.text: Failed to save the service log policy.

intro.text: Download Agents and settings files for this AIC Server instance. CMMC in a Box is the integrated toolkit. Installing an Agent does not certify the organisation.

inventoryPurpose.text: These Agents inventory seats and validate the required state for the CMMC standard in effect. The standard in effect is the configured operating package ({{package}}). Inventory and required-state validation are product contribution. They are not Met, they do not certify a seat, and they do not replace the assessor.

inventoryPurposeUnset.text: These Agents inventory seats and validate the required state for the CMMC standard in effect. The operating package is not set. Choose L1 Fast, L2 Isolated, L3 Overlay, or NIST SP 800-53 in Settings. Until then, Agents still inventory seats; required-state validation follows the package you configure. Inventory and required-state validation are product contribution. They are not Met, they do not certify a seat, and they do not replace the assessor.

honesty.text: Inventory and required-state validation are product contribution (Live or Partial). They are not Met, not a certified seat, and not a substitute for the assessor.

settingsBody.text: The settings file is not a generic configuration list. It carries unique cryptographic material that starts the initial secure connection. After the Agent enrols and checks in, the server updates that material and pushes the remaining settings. The user interface never shows private keys, PINs, or tokens.

settingsWizard.text: Open the settings wizard to build a per-machine unique configuration file for the installer.

installersHelp.text: Each row is a shipping installer this instance can serve. Version and SHA-256 come from the file on disk. Missing platforms stay blocked. This server does not invent binaries or hashes.

downloadFailed.text: Could not download that installer. Confirm the file is still in the instance share, then retry.

blocked.text: Blocked — no file on this instance

loadFailed.text: Could not load the Agents Download catalogue.

whereBody.text: After check-in, seats appear on Systems, Fleet Agent Versions, and Workstation Assurance. Elevation and recording surfaces use the Agent that is already on the seat. Those pages show delivery state, not Met.

whyBody.text: Agents provide endpoint presence, check-in, inventory, and required-state evidence for the operating package in effect. That is toolkit contribution. It does not mean the organisation passed an assessment.
